3.2.5.1-r2.burton_quote: are full of bad spirits and Devils, devilish thoughts; no better Physic for such parties, than to fast

3.2.5.1-r3.burton_quote: as severely punished for drinking of wine, as for adultery

3.2.5.1-r4.burton_quote: A Lover that hath as it were lost himself through impotency, impatience, must be called home as a traveller by music, feasting, good wine, if need be, to drunkenness itself, which many so much commend for the easing of the mind, all kinds of sports and merriments, to see fair pictures, hangings, buildings, pleasant fields, Orchards, Gardens, Groves, ponds, pools, Rivers, fishing, fowling, hawking, hunting, to hear merry tales, and pleasant discourse, reading, to use exercise till he sweat

3.2.5.1-r5.burton_quote: letting themselves blood under the ears, and to make both men and women barren
